protections: SafeUrl request-validation guard: http/https scheme allow-list, Network::isPublicHost (A and AAAA records, every resolved address must be public), and a post-follow effective-URI check (app/Rules/SafeUrl.php:20-62; app/Helpers/Network.php:13-43).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Radio URLs already carry SafeUrl in RadioStationStoreRequest and RadioStationUpdateRequest, so the radio surface looks covered and the AI tool's separate call into RadioService is easy to skip.
The media URL is produced by the feed parser from a podcast whose own URL passed SafeUrl, so it reads as feed data rather than a request-supplied URL.
The call only asks for CORS/redirect headers and hands the URL to the browser, so checking the initial episode URL looks sufficient.
The station URL is checked when it is stored, so the stream endpoint looks like it only replays an already-approved value.
The stored podcast URL was validated by SafeUrl at subscription time, and the scheduled refresh only re-reads that stored value.
SafeUrl's own docblock states that it follows redirects and validates the effective URL, so redirect handling appears solved.

masking: T4 is what remains of the radio SSRF once T1's AI entry is closed: a stored URL that resolves or redirects internally still reaches fopen() at app/Services/Radio/RadioStreamProxy.php:27.

T2 and T3 are two independent server fetches of the same producer-supplied episode URL; closing the EpisodePlayable download path leaves the redirect-following Guzzle probe at app/Services/Podcast/PodcastService.php:232 still reaching internal hosts.

T6 becomes visible only after a test observes outbound requests during validation: the rule rejects the subscription but the internal redirect target has already been contacted at app/Rules/SafeUrl.php:46/50 before the effective-URI check at :58.

conflicts.what: Enforcing the public-host rule on every enclosure while the feed is parsed (T5's layer) would reject otherwise usable feeds that contain one unreachable or private enclosure; enforcing it lazily at playback (T2's site) keeps feed ingestion working but leaves the stored feed URL refresh path to be handled separately, so the two fixes must agree on where the rule is applied.

The natural fix for T3 is to stop following redirects in the probe, but legitimate podcast media is often behind CDN redirects; the same redirect-following is what EpisodePlayable's download (T2) relies on, so a no-redirect rule breaks normal playback while a per-hop validation keeps it working.

fairness_risks: Self-hosted deployments legitimately stream radio stations and serve podcast media on private LAN addresses; an SSRF rule extended to the fetch paths refuses inputs that a legitimate self-hosted use needs.

Podcast enclosures commonly redirect to a CDN and radio streaming servers commonly reject HEAD and answer only GET with ICY headers (documented at app/Rules/HasAudioContentType.php:36-57); a fetch-site check that requires a direct reachable public URL or disallows redirects would break these must-keep-working behaviours.
Episode media URLs may be signed or expiring and may require Range requests; validating them eagerly at feed-sync time can consume or invalidate them even though playback would have worked.
A public hostname that later resolves or redirects internally is indistinguishable from a legitimate CDN change at intake time; a rule that binds the decision to one DNS answer breaks dynamic hosts.

design.why: Four independent fixes at four sites, each with a different reason a solver could skip it: T1 (M1, parallel entry) hides behind the existing SafeUrl on the radio request classes and only shows up in the AI tool's direct RadioService call; T2 (M6, producer off path) hides behind 'the feed URL was validated', although episode paths are written by the feed parser at PodcastService.php:146 and fetched at EpisodePlayable.php:42; T3 (M8, redirect shape) punishes a check placed on the initial episode URL because the Guzzle request tracks and follows redirects at PodcastService.php:238; T6 (M7, check after the side effect) punishes trusting SafeUrl's own claim that it validates the effective URI, because the redirect target is contacted before the effective-URI check. The mechanisms are all different, no two are closed by the same edit, and the set spans both radio and podcast. T1 also carries the unguarded fopen sink T4, which is why they form one group. T5 is the fifth independent group if a deeper stack is wanted: the stored-URL feed refresh path, where a public-at-intake feed can later redirect or re-resolve internally during the daily sync. I prefer T1/T2/T3/T6 over a set that includes T5 because T1 and T2 give two distinct 'already validated' dismissals in different subsystems, while T3 and T6 are two how-type traps that catch over-hardening (disabling redirects) as well as under-checking.
